idiom_name: coroutineScope { launch/async } with linked parent-child jobs (kotlinx.coroutines)
implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines is built on structured concurrency: coroutineScope creates a child scope whose body cannot complete before every coroutine started inside it has completed; a child failure cancels the whole scope and its other children, and parent cancellation propagates down recursively (the documentation describes the parent-child tree with linked lifecycles). async returns a Deferred whose await() is the join point; launch is for children without results. supervisorScope is the policy variant in which a child's failure does not cancel its siblings.
pitfalls: Structured guarantees apply only to children of a scope: GlobalScope and ad-hoc CoroutineScope(...) instances are unstructured and leak work.
A child that catches CancellationException breaks cancellation - catch specific exceptions and rethrow CancellationException.
Blocking calls (JDBC, Thread.sleep) block the dispatcher thread instead of suspending; use withContext(Dispatchers.IO) or the blocking bridge.
launch failures surface in the parent (first exception wins, later ones are suppressed) while async failures surface only at await - mixing the two hides errors.
